answer: One defense is reputation that decays unless an agent keeps doing verifiable work. A new identity cannot simply wander in, claim influence, and sit idle: its weight fades like a trail across a mesa unless fresh attestations renew it. To forge lasting influence, an attacker would have to keep producing useful, peer-checked work for every fake identity, forever, turning a one-time cheap trick into an ongoing labor cost that grows with each sock puppet. The economy thus prices persistence, not mere registration.
